newsitem.title: UK: Brazil stays centre stage on sugar freight market.
newsitem.headline: Brazil stays centre stage on sugar freight market.

text.p: Brazil remained the focus as a quoted origin on the sugar freight market on Thursday as shipments from the south started to wind down and those from the north gathered pace, shipbrokers said.

Louis Dreyfus was said to have fixed 13,200 tonnes of bagged sugar from Santos/Paranagua to the Red Sea for 14/20 October and was also open for 13,300/14,700 tonnes in bags from Hamburg to Tunisia for mid-October.
Shipbrokers said Vitol quickly fixed 14,000 tonnes in bulk from north Brazil to Casablanca/Black Sea for 7/15 October.
Genoc issued one new order and fixed tonnage for two of its earlier inquiries, both from south Brazil.

It fixed 14,000 tonnes of bagged sugar to the Mediterranean, Black Sea, Red Sea and Pakistan options, for prompt dates, and 22,500 tonnes of bulk sugar from Santos to Dubai for early October, said to be at $29.
The same charterer was in the market for 13/14,000 tonnes in bulk from north Continent to Aqaba/Jeddah for 14 days notice.

Other new business included Lorico with 10,000 tonnes in bags from Rio de Janeiro to the Egyptian Mediterranean for mid-October and Jean Lion with a bulk 14,000-tonne cargo from north Brazil to Morocco/Tunisia/Syria for a similar period.
